Pottery Seminar with Shoji Hamada

A seminar held from October 15 to 29, 1952, together with a fall Crafts Institute. The prospectus announced a tuition fee of a hundred dollars. Karnes watches Shoji Hamada work there: his Japanese aesthetic and his way of working at the wheel influence her later forms and decorative sensibility.

Two books on the female nude arrive

One sunny afternoon, in a house full of mostly male painters, two books arrive: The Female Form in Painting (Cassou and Grigson) and Nus d'Autrefois (Bovis and St. Julien); the book of photographs at first eclipses the book of paintings.
